title: Pushforward and pullback of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]),
with pulled-back coefficient rings $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$
([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]), categories of module objects
$\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]) and coefficient morphisms
$\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$, $\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to f^{\Ab}_*\Lambda_X$
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]) for morphisms of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$.
Everything below is stated for a general
$\Lambda$; the $\ell$-adic rings, including $\underline{\Qlb}$, are instances.
Write $f^{\Ab}_*$ and $f^*_{\Ab}$ for the pushforward and pullback of sheaves of
abelian groups ([def-sfb-finite-lower-star], [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], with $\mathcal A=\Ab$);
$f^{\Ab}_*$ is lax monoidal ([def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal]) and
$f^*_{\Ab}$ is strong monoidal ([def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]), so both transport
module objects ([sk-def-sfb-transport]); applied to ring objects such as
$\Lambda_Y$, the symbols $f^*$ and $f_*$ always mean these functors of abelian
sheaves. Every functor on module objects is "transport
the $\Ab$-valued functor, then change scalars along $\eta_f$ or $\alpha_f$"
([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]). For a morphism of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$:

- the *pushforward*
  $$
  f_*:=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)\colon
  \Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Y};
  $$
  the underlying sheaf of $f_*M$ is $f^{\Ab}_*M$, with $\Lambda_Y$ acting through
  $\eta_f$, and $f_*$ is additive and left exact;
- the *pullback*
  $$
  f^*:=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\colon
  \Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X},
  \qquad f^*M=\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M,
  $$
  the ringed-topos pullback. The extension of scalars along $\alpha_f$ is kept
  although $\alpha_f$ is invertible, so that the definition is the standard one and
  does not depend on a choice of inverse;
- the *adjunction* $f^*\dashv f_*$: the lift of the monoidal adjunction
  $f^*_{\Ab}\dashv f^{\Ab}_*$ to module objects, composed with
  $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f}$, using that
  $\eta_f$ is the mate of $\alpha_f$;
- for $g\colon Y\to Z$, the *composition isomorphisms*
  $$
  g_*\circ f_*\cong(g\circ f)_*,\qquad (g\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ g^*,
  $$
  the first lifting the composition isomorphism of pushforwards of abelian sheaves,
  the second deduced from the first by uniqueness of left adjoints.

The constructions use only $\alpha_f$, $\eta_f$ and the mate relation between
them; that $\alpha_f$ is invertible enters proofs about these functors (exactness,
the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$), not their definitions.

proof.text: Take $f_*$ from [def-sfb-module-lower-star]: its action on $f_*^{\Ab}M$ is $f_*^{\Ab}(\gamma_M)\mu(\eta_f\otimes1)$, and it is additive and left exact. Take $f^*$ from [def-sfb-module-upper-star], giving $\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M$. Both definitions act on morphisms as transport followed by the indicated scalar change, with the forward $\alpha_f$.

Apply [lem-sfb-coefficient-mate-module-hom-comparison] with $F=f^*_{\Ab}$, $G=f_*^{\Ab}$, $B=\Lambda_Y$, $A=\Lambda_X$, $\alpha=\alpha_f$. Use the sheaf adjunction [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] with mate monoidal structures [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal], and the scalar adjunction [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The mate formula in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] is $\eta_f=G(\alpha_f)u_B$. Thus the lemma identifies the composite right adjoint with step 1 by the identity on underlying sheaves and gives exactly the required natural Hom bijection. This is the construction of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction].

For $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, let $P=f_*^{\Ab}$, $Q=g_*^{\Ab}$, $H=(gf)_*^{\Ab}$. Their composition comparison $c:QP\cong H$ is monoidal by [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal]. Apply [lem-sfb-eta-comp] to obtain $\eta_{gf}=c_{\Lambda_X}Q(\eta_f)\eta_g$. Its conventions apply: [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp] is the conjugate of $c$; [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso] takes its inverse at $(h,\pi_B)$ and precomposes with $p^*$; [def-sfb-alpha] evaluates at $\Lambda$. These are precisely the $m_{h,\pi_B}$ and $\alpha_h$ used by the eta lemma.

Apply [lem-sfb-restricted-transport-comparison-linear] with $F=P$, $G=Q$, $H$, $e=c$, $A=\Lambda_X$, $B=\Lambda_Y$, $B'=\Lambda_Z$, $\psi=\eta_f$, $\psi'=\eta_g$, $\varphi=\eta_{gf}$: $c$ is monoidal and $\varphi=c_AQ(\psi)\psi'$ by step 3, and [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] supplies ring morphisms; so each $c_M$ is $\Lambda_Z$-linear. Then apply [lem-sfb-coefficient-composition-module-comparison] with these $P,Q,H,c$, $A,B,C=\Lambda_X,\Lambda_Y,\Lambda_Z$ and $(\psi,\chi,\varphi)=(\eta_f,\eta_g,\eta_{gf})$; its linearity hypothesis is the one just obtained. Step 1 identifies $T_P,T_Q,T_H$ with the module pushforwards. The lemma yields their natural module isomorphism with underlying $c_M,c_M^{-1}$. With the adjunctions of step 2, it also gives $(gf)^*\cong f^*g^*$, with conjugate $\delta$ and the stated unit equation.

proof.text: These comparisons are [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp] and [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp], respectively, by their specified underlying comparison and conjugate. Finally [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] gives invertibility of $\alpha_f$; neither extracted lemma assumes it. Extension along the forward morphism is therefore retained uniformly for all commutative condensed $\Lambda$.
